architectural_shifts: From a single global linear control-variate weight (PPI/PPI++) to a nonparametric calibrated control variate g(Yhat) fit by cross-fitting
From one cross-fit to repeated cross-fit with stacked calibrators
From label-based calibration to a label-free basis control variate (did not beat calibration)
benchmarks: ppi-python example data: galaxies (Galaxy Zoo 2 spiral labels)
reference_query_plan.central_topic: Whether confidence intervals for a population mean can be shortened, at valid nominal coverage, beyond prediction-powered inference when labels, unlabeled data and the pretrained predictor are all fixed, using cross-fitted recalibration of the predictor output as a control variate.
comparators: Double/debiased ML and semiparametric efficient estimation with missing outcomes
core_methods: Cross-fitted recalibrated PPI mean intervals (isotonic / binned / stacked calibrators g(Yhat) fit on labeled data)
Repeated cross-fitting with NNLS-stacked calibrator library and split-dispersion variance
Label-free spline-basis control-variate PPI with PRESS selection (weaker result)
Power-tuned PPI++ shrinkage with PPI++ fallback selection
Efficiency-bound / semiparametric theory for the mean with auxiliary predictions

queries.rationale: Cross-fitted nuisance estimation with debiased inference motivates the recalibration step and its validity argument.
Isotonic and binned calibrators are the main recalibration maps g(Yhat) in the best-scoring method.

queries.rationale: PPI++ and recalibration are control-variate / model-assisted estimators; connects width gains to classical difference and regression estimators.

queries.rationale: Dataset provenance for the ppi-python example data used in evaluation; to be split by the retriever into separate dataset lookups.

result_driven_themes: Width gains over PPI++ are small on real datasets (log width ratio about 0.003-0.03) but larger on synthetic nonlinear miscalibration (about 0.07)
Large gain over the classical interval (log ratio about 0.47-0.49) confirms the predictor is informative
Coverage stays near nominal (pooled about 0.94-0.95) with small-n finite-sample issues, motivating t-reference and variance-estimation corrections
Predictor miscalibration limits how much PPI++ can gain; recalibration helps only when the Yhat-Y relation is nonlinear
